ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: ams1 control-plane heartbeat gap detected (missing ~45s). Affected: inference-api, autoscaler. severity=high. runbook: /runbooks/region-heartbeat.md

alex: Oncall — I see the alert. Anyone already on the control-plane nodes? :eyes:

maya: I'm on it. Starting quick health probes and kube events. Sending logs in a sec.

liam: Running quick pod check now — hitting the cluster via bastion.
liam: ```
kubectl get pods -n control-plane -o wide
NAME               READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
controller-0       1/1     Running   0          12d
controller-1       1/1     Running   0          12d
controller-2       0/1     Unknown   1          5m
```

netty: Seeing network interface flaps on controller-2 from host logs (NIC resets). Might be switch-level or SR-IOV hiccup. Traceroute to other nodes shows intermittent drops.

alex: Can we confirm controlplane leader? If leader is down, global scheduler might consider region degraded.

maya: ```
kubectl -n control-plane logs controller-2 --tail=100
E0421 12:34:38.123 main.go:45] heartbeat: lost connection to etcd cluster: EOF
E0421 12:34:40.456 main.go:45] kube-apiserver: received sigterm
```

liam: Etcd connection flapping on that node. I can try to restart the kubelet on controller-2, but NIC flaps worry me. netty, any chance to move the instance to a different host?

netty: I'm checking with cloud provider. If it's a noisy neighbor or host-level networking problem we'll need a live migration or to drain and reprovision. ETA on provider reply ~8-12 mins.

alex: We should avoid full region failover immediately. Can we shift non-critical traffic off ams1 while we triage? Suggest moving inference batch jobs and lower-priority routes to eu-central1, keep user-facing latency-sensitive endpoints on healthy nodes only.

liam: Agreed. I can create a temporary routing policy: `--weight ams1=75,eu-central1=25` for the next 30m. Command: `redwoodctl routes update inference --weights ams1=75,eu-central1=25 --reason "ams1 heartbeat gap"`

sophie: Heads up on capacity: eu-central1 has spare capacity for ~30% traffic before we hit our reserved capacity. If we shift too much we'll incur burst instances in dedicated pools and higher cost. Recommend 20-25% shift for now.

alex: OK let's do 25% shift. liam, execute and monitor for errors and 5xx rate. Add a circuit-breaker so we can revert if errors spike.

liam: Running: `redwoodctl routes update inference --weights ams1=75,eu-central1=25 --circuit-breaker=5%` — API returned 202. :thumbsup:

maya: Monitoring: initial 5xx bump nil, latency stable. kube-events for controller-2 still noisy. Provider says host NIC has been rebooted and they're performing host maintenance — may cause additional node restarts.

netty: Provider confirmed host-level NIC driver issue; they are moving workloads off host. We should plan full node reprovision if controller-2 doesn't come up cleanly after migration.

alex: Escalating: OPEN incident to SOC and infra-eng; tagging pager for node provisioning. Adding severity=high and timeline.

sophie: Logging note: I'm enabling additional retention for control-plane logs for next 72h for postmortem.

maya: Next steps: 1) Keep 25% traffic diverted for 1h and reassess 2) If controller-2 fails post-migration, reprovision from snapshot and join cluster 3) Run cluster health checks and run load test on failover path.

alex: Agreed. I'll update the incident board and notify CS for customer status updates. If error rate >2% or latency +200ms, we'll escalate to full region failover plan.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-AMS1-0912. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2024-AMS1-0912

liam: Monitoring traffic now. Will post updates every 5-10m or earlier if things change.

alex: thanks team — good containment so far. :white_check_mark:
